## Purpose

Inspect the evidence for a morning report without reserving a report or waking
its author. The CLI entry point is `aq report morning --dry-run --json`.

## When a playbook uses it

Use this read to inspect coverage and evidence before enabling daily delivery.
Scheduling and author requests are separate commands introduced in later plans.

## How it works internally

`src/commands/report_commands.py` validates UTC epoch bounds and narrows the
configured project selection to the authenticated principal. With no explicit
end, it uses the most recent 07:00 boundary in `reports.timezone`; the first
window is 24 hours, capped at 72. Schedule configuration is deferred.

`src/reports/queries.py` reads completions (including archived task identities),
development deliveries, recovery incidents, escalations, failed session attempts,
provider transitions, reroutes and digest context in one PostgreSQL read-only,
repeatable-read snapshot. Sources are capped at 500 rows and 100 projects.
Savepoints preserve the snapshot after an individual source failure.

`src/reports/git.py` reads a configured base repository with frozen object ids,
ancestry checks and bounded log/diffstat output. It never uses the worker cwd,
fetches or runs an author-supplied expression. Remote observations carry freshness
warnings; missing objects and divergent history are gaps. A first observation
has no previous head and cannot prove a complete landing interval.

`src/reports/morning.py` builds a versioned 24 KiB brief and canonical hash using
the shared REPORT hash primitive. Project sections reference landed, pending and
failed evidence. A completion or PR URL is not shipment proof. Verification is
labelled agent-reported. Manual-check authoring and live CI collection are not
part of this preview; CI's absence is explicit in coverage warnings.

## Side effects and persistence

No rows, files, watermarks, messages or deliveries are written; no model is
called. Preview can be repeated without consuming coverage. The collector accepts
morning fact membership and previous heads from future schedule code, rescans
72 hours for late facts, and proposes cursors/heads only for successfully read
sources. Hourly digest membership is context, never morning deduplication.

## Failure modes and diagnostics

`out_of_scope` rejects a selection outside the principal or configured visibility;
`report.invalid` rejects bad bounds or unknown project ids;
`report.source_unavailable` means the read-only snapshot could not be established.
Individual failures and limits appear under `brief.coverage.gaps`; they prevent
no-change suppression and advancement of that source. Lateness beyond 72 hours is
explicitly unsupported. An oversized brief reports omissions and proposes no
coverage advancement.

## Example step

```yaml
id: inspect-morning
kind: command
command: morning_report_preview
args:
  since: 1790233200
  until: 1790319600
  project_ids: [agent-queue]
```
